author: reek
body: The positive half of the `Real trapping` contract: a result that leaves the finite range must trap.

author: reek
body: It traps with `UD2`, so this program dies rather than printing, and there is no output to compare. That is why it carries a `.fatal` sidecar and no `.expected`, the same arrangement `bounded-param-trap` and `bounded-return-trap` use for the same reason.

author: reek
body: The line before the overflow prints, so a run that produces `alive` and then dies on `!EXC=06` is the trap firing at the right place. A run that prints `alive` and then a bit pattern is the guard failing to fire, which is the defect this test exists for: the emitter checked for NaN alone and let every infinity through.
